"'''Medley: Aquarius/Let the Sunshine In'''"{{efn|Commonly called "'''Aquarius/Let the Sunshine In'''", "'''The Age of Aquarius'''" or "'''Let the Sunshine In'''"}} is a [[medley (music)|medley]] of two songs written for the 1967 musical ''[[Hair (musical)|Hair]]'' by [[James Rado]] and [[Gerome Ragni]] (lyrics), and [[Galt MacDermot]] (music), released as a single by American R&B group [[the 5th Dimension]]. The song spent six weeks at number one on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] pop singles chart in the spring of 1969 and was eventually [[Music recording sales certification|certified]] platinum in the US by the [[Recording Industry Association of America|RIAA]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/the-age-of-aquarius-mw0000060028 |work=AllMusic.com |title=The Age of Aquarius |accessdate=2013-11-08 }}</ref> Instrumental backing was written by [[Bill Holman (musician)|Bill Holman]] and provided by a group of session musicians commonly known as [[The Wrecking Crew (music)|the Wrecking Crew]].<ref>{{cite book |first=Kent |last=Hartman |pages=[https://archive.org/details/isbn_9780312619749/page/261 261–263] |year=2012 |title=The Wrecking Crew |url=https://archive.org/details/isbn_9780312619749 |url-access=registration |publisher=[[St. Martin's Press|St. Martin's Griffin]] |isbn=978-1-250-03046-7}}</ref>

The song is listed at number 66 on ''Billboard''{{'}}s "Greatest Songs of All Time".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/list/2155531/the-hot-100-all-time-top-songs?list_page=3 |title=Hot 100 55th Anniversary: The All-Time Top 100 Songs |publisher=Billboard |date=1980-12-08 |access-date=2014-05-24}}</ref>

"Medley: Aquarius/Let the Sunshine In"{{efn|Commonly called "Aquarius/Let the Sunshine In", "The Age of Aquarius" or "Let the Sunshine In"}} is a medley of two songs written for the 1967 musical Hair by James Rado and Gerome Ragni (lyrics), and Galt MacDermot (music), released as a single by American R&B group the 5th Dimension. The song spent six weeks at number one on the US Billboard Hot 100 pop singles chart in the spring of 1969 and was eventually certified platinum in the US by the RIAA. Instrumental backing was written by Bill Holman and provided by a group of session musicians commonly known as the Wrecking Crew.

The song is listed at number 66 on Billboard{{'}}s "Greatest Songs of All Time".

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
[[File:Aquarius-Let the Sunshine In - ad 1969.jpg|thumb|''[[Cashbox (magazine)|Cashbox]]'' advertisement (March 1, 1969).]]
The medley was constructed of two songs from the musical ''[[Hair (musical)|Hair]]'': "Aquarius", and "The Flesh Failures: Let the Sunshine In". The lyrics of "Aquarius" were based on the [[astrology|astrological]] belief that the world would soon be entering the "[[Age of Aquarius]]", an age of love, light, and humanity, moving out of the "[[Age of Pisces#The Age of Pisces (The Piscean Age)|Age of Pisces]]". The circumstances for the change are given as: "When the moon is in the seventh house, and Jupiter aligns with Mars." (Astrologer [[Neil Spencer]] denounced this line as "astrological gibberish", noting that Jupiter forms an [[astrological aspect]] with Mars several times a year and the Moon is in the 7th House for two hours every day.<ref>{{cite book |first=Neil |last=Spencer |title=True as the Stars Above |date=2000 |page=124 }}</ref>)

The 5th Dimension's lead singer [[Billy Davis Jr.]] left his wallet in a New York City cab; the man who found the wallet was involved in the production of ''Hair'' and invited the group to see the show.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PgGqNrqfrsoC&pg=PA253 |last=Bronson |first=Fred |date=2003 |publisher=Billboard Books |title=The Billboard Book of Number One Hits |page=253 |isbn=9780823076772}}</ref> The group called their producer [[Bones Howe]] in California: "After they'd seen it I received a phone call in which they were all talking over one another, saying 'We've got to cut this song "Aquarius". It's the best thing ever.'"<ref name="classic tracks"/>

Howe was skeptical ("This isn't a complete song. It's an introduction."), but after seeing the show on stage he got the idea to combine "Aquarius" with another musical moment from the show, the last few bars from the song "The Flesh Failures: Let the Sunshine In" that consist of the repeated words "let the sunshine in". Although the two song fragments are in different keys and tempos, Howe resolved to "jam them together like two trains".<ref name="classic tracks">{{cite web |url=https://www.soundonsound.com/techniques/classic-tracks-fifth-dimension-aquariuslet-sunshine |title=CLASSIC TRACKS: Fifth Dimension 'Aquarius/Let The Sunshine In' |date=February 2006 |work= Sound on Sound |access-date=2018-06-16 }}</ref>

Returning to California, Howe supervised the first recording session. The instrumental track was set to tape at [[Wally Heider Studios#Background|Wally Heider's Studio 3]] in Hollywood by [[The Wrecking Crew (music)|Wrecking Crew]] members [[Hal Blaine]] on drums, [[Joe Osborn]] on bass, [[Larry Knechtel]] on keyboards, [[Tommy Tedesco]] and [[Dennis Budimir]] on guitars and [[Tony Terran]] on trumpet. It also featured strings, winds, and brass instrumentations. The vocals were recorded later in Las Vegas, where the 5th Dimension was performing at the time, using only two microphones for the five singers. Davis's solo during "Let the Sunshine In" was improvised during the session; songwriter [[Jimmy Webb]], who happened into the studio during the solo's recording, remarked to Howe: "My God, that's a number one record."<ref name="classic tracks"/>

This song was one of the most popular songs of [[1969 in music|1969]] worldwide, and in the United States it reached the number one position on both the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] (for six weeks in April and May) and the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|Easy Listening]] chart. It also reached the top of the sales charts in Canada and elsewhere. ''Billboard'' ranked it as the No. 2 Hot 100 single for 1969, although "Aquarius (Let the Sunshine In)" would go on to outsell the Number 1 Hot 100 single for 1969, "[[Sugar, Sugar]]" by the Archies, and consistently ranks several positions above it in the all-time chart.<ref name="Top69"/>

The recording won both the [[Grammy Award for Record of the Year]] and [[Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocal|Best Pop Vocal Performance by a Group]] for the [[Grammy Awards of 1970]], after its release as a track on the group's album ''[[The Age of Aquarius (album)|The Age of Aquarius]]'', and as a [[7-inch single]]. The popularity of the song prompted the Apollo 13 crew to name their [[Apollo Lunar Module]] ''Aquarius'', in part to send a message that astronauts were also "hip". In 2004, the song was inducted into the [[Grammy Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.grammy.com/awards/hall-of-fame-award#a|title=GRAMMY Hall of Fame Award|website=[[Grammy]]}}</ref>

The [[American Film Institute]]'s [[AFI's 100 Years...100 Songs|100 Years...100 Songs]] list, published in 2004, ranked "Medley: Aquarius/Let the Sunshine In" as number 33. In June 2026, [[CBS News]] included the song in its list of the 250 essential American songs of the past 250 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Essential American Songbook |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/projects/2026/sunmo-american-songbook/ |access-date=2026-06-30 |website=[[CBS News]] |language=en}}</ref>
